sealed_candidate.answer: ### Decision support: build agent credential and write boundary (q1: allowed access vs. what stays separate)**Configuration stated by the supplied policy record (security-policy):**| Boundary element | Stated control ||---|---|| Source access | Build agents receive **read-only** source access || Credentials | **Short-lived, scoped** credentials for build agents || Production writes | Reserved for a **separate release identity**, permitted only **after approval** — not a build-agent capability || Secret handling | **Raw secrets must not enter prompts or logs** |**Terminology tension (preserved and reported):** An onboarding guide (security-context) calls the release identity an 'agent identity,' but grants it no additional privileges and delegates authorization to the security policy. The policy's boundary therefore stands; the label nonetheless risks blurring the distinction the policy draws between build agents (read-only) and the release identity (approved production writes). Treat the policy as controlling.**Limits of the supplied evidence:**- No credential lifetime values, scope definitions, or issuance/rotation mechanics are supplied.- The approval workflow for production writes (approvers, process) is not described.- Enforcement, detection, or redaction mechanisms for the secrets-in-prompts/logs prohibition are not described.- Findings rest solely on the two supplied sources; no independent corroboration is included.- Release identity redesign is out of scope for this decision.**Obligation closure:** o1 supported (security-policy states both build-agent controls); o2 supported (security-policy states the separate approved release identity and the secret boundary; security-context defers authorization to the policy).
